questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses **inversion** to emphasise the subject in a conditional clause?
options: If she **hadn’t** been tired, she would have finished the report yesterday.
Had she been tired, she wouldn’t have finished the report yesterday.
She would have finished the report yesterday if she hadn’t been tired.
She would have finished the report yesterday, had she been tired.
questions.answer: Had she been tired, she wouldn’t have finished the report yesterday.

questions.question: Which sentence uses **cleft structure** to focus on the reason for an action?
options: It was because of the meeting that she missed her flight.
Because of the meeting, she missed her flight.
The reason she missed her flight was the meeting.
She missed her flight due to the meeting.
questions.answer: It was because of the meeting that she missed her flight.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses **advanced subjunctive** to express a hypothetical scenario with a formal tone?
options: She insists that he **be** invited to the conference tomorrow.
She insists that he **is** invited to the conference tomorrow.
She insists that he **was** invited to the conference tomorrow.
She insists that he **be** invited to the conference yesterday.
questions.answer: She insists that he **be** invited to the conference tomorrow.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates **ellipsis** in a complex conditional structure?
options: If you had told me earlier, I would have helped you.
If you had told me, I would have helped.
If you told me earlier, I would have helped you.
If you had told me, I would have helped you too.
questions.answer: If you had told me, I would have helped.

questions.question: Which sentence uses **formal register** and **complex sentence structure** to express a nuanced opinion about a policy?
options: The government’s new tax policy is too complicated; it will confuse the public.
While the government’s new tax policy aims to simplify taxation, its implementation risks alienating those who previously relied on existing systems.
Taxes are complicated; the government should make changes.
The public will understand the new tax policy if it is explained clearly.
questions.answer: While the government’s new tax policy aims to simplify taxation, its implementation risks alienating those who previously relied on existing systems.
